'''Marek Fila''' (29  August 1959 – 20 April 2023)<ref>{{cite web |title=Accreditation material of FMFI |url=https://fmph.uniba.sk/fileadmin/fmfi/fakulta/akademicky_senat/plenum/2007_2008/14/04-D_9-1-9_Aplikovana_matematika.pdf |access-date=24 April 2023}}</ref> was a Slovak mathematician. His main research focus was [[Diffusion equation|diffusion equations]] and [[Partial differential equation|partial differential equations]]. He was among the most productive scientists in Slovakia.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Richtárik |first1=Peter |title=Slovenskí vedci a vedkyne s vysokým Hirschovým indexom |url=https://www.slovenskivedci.sk/zoznam.html |website=www.slovenskivedci.sk |access-date=24 April 2023}}</ref> 

Fila was born in [[Bratislava]] to an artistic family. His father was the painter [[Rudolf Fila]] and his mother [[Dorota Filová]] was a well-known renovator of medieval art.<ref name="N_Kol">{{cite web |last1=Kollár |first1=Richard |title=Za Marekom Filom |url=https://dennikn.sk/3339263/za-marekom-filom/?ref=list |website=Denník N |access-date=24 April 2023 |language=sk-SK |date=23 April 2023}}</ref>

Fila studied Mathematics at the [[Comenius University]], graduating in 1989. His doctoral advisor was [[Pavol Brunovský]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Marek Fila - The Mathematics Genealogy Project |url=https://www.mathgenealogy.org/id.php?id=122294 |website=www.mathgenealogy.org |access-date=24 April 2023}}</ref> Following his graduation, he remained at the university and became a full professor in 2008.<ref>{{cite web |title=Osoby, ktoré získali titul na UK |url=https://absolventi.uniba.sk/searchTop.do |website=absolventi.uniba.sk}}</ref> In the 1990s, he was a visiting researcher at the [[Iowa State University]] and later a recurrent visitor at the [[University of Tokyo]].<ref name="N_Kol" /> He founded the Department of Applied Mathematics and Statistics at the Faculty of Mathematics and Physics of the Comenius University and led it for 11 years.<ref name="death_anonc" /> 

Fila had two children; son [[Lukáš Fila]], who is a journalist and musician, and daughter Natália, who is an architect.<ref name="N_Kol" /> 

Fila's death was announced by his department on the faculty website on 23 April 2023.<ref name="death_anonc">{{cite web |title=Opustil nás prof. Marek Fila |url=https://fmph.uniba.sk/detail-novinky/article/opustil-nas-prof-marek-fila/ |website=fmph.uniba.sk |access-date=24 April 2023 |language=sk-SK}}</ref>
